t: In a one-party state a single party controls government by law or in practice; other parties are banned or allowed only as junior allies, and elections offer no real choice of rulers.
The form began in Soviet Russia between 1918 and 1921, spread to Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany, and after 1945 to the communist states and many newly independent countries in Africa and Asia.
Most one-party states became multi-party systems after 1989–1991, but communist parties still rule China, Vietnam, Laos, Cuba and North Korea, and dominant-party systems remain common.
dyk: Article 6 of the Soviet constitution of 1977 named the Communist Party “the leading and guiding force of Soviet society”; its amendment in March 1990 ended the party’s legal monopoly less than two years before the Soviet Union dissolved.
ev: The Bolsheviks dissolve the Constituent Assembly and expel rival socialist parties from the soviets
The Tenth Congress of the Russian Communist Party bans factions as the last rival parties are suppressed
Mussolini’s government dissolves every party except the National Fascist Party
Germany’s Law against the Formation of New Parties makes the Nazi Party the only legal party
The Chinese Communist Party wins the civil war and proclaims the People’s Republic of China on 1 October
Tanzania becomes a one-party state by law, with rival candidates of the ruling party in most constituencies
The Soviet Union amends Article 6 of its constitution, ending the Communist Party’s monopoly of power
Mexico’s Institutional Revolutionary Party loses the presidency after 71 years in power

f.power: The ruling party’s leadership, usually a politburo or central committee and the party leader, whose decisions the organs of the state carry out
f.legitimacy: An official ideology or national mission, such as building socialism, national rebirth or independence and development, which the party claims alone to embody
f.chosen: Leaders rise through the party hierarchy and are chosen by its congresses and committees; elections, where held, offer only candidates the party approves
f.examples: The Soviet Union, Fascist Italy, Nazi Germany, Turkey under the Republican People’s Party, the People’s Republic of China, Tanzania under Julius Nyerere
